# Adjudication Task — Chapter 543

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃543화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|쿵. 쿵.
  6|
  7|지축을 울리는 발걸음에 길을 지나가던 사람들이 좌우로 길을 텄다.
  8|
  9|그리고 그들의 경계 어린 눈빛이 자신의 옆에 있는 태산의 존재 때문이 아님을, 흑룡도 사마표는 알고 있었다.
 10|
 11|‘우리에 관한 소문이 꽤 퍼진 모양이로군.’
 12|
 13|하긴, 알려지지 않는 것이 이상한 일이다.
 14|
 15|옆 골목 담벼락에 기대어 꾸벅꾸벅 졸고 있는 거지의 허리춤에는 누렇게 찌든 매듭이 삐죽 튀어나와 있고, 날아드는 파리를 쫓는 좌판 상인의 손바닥에는 희미한 굳은살이 박여 있었다.
 16|
 17|‘개방, 하오문.’
 18|
 19|당장 눈에 보이는 것만 해도 이 정도다.
 20|
 21|하남 어디를 가도 수많은 이목이 지켜보는 상황이니 아마 오늘 자신의 행보도 반나절이 채 지나기도 전에 여러 인물에게 알려질 것이 분명했다.
 22|
 23|‘숨길 생각도 없었지만.’
 24|
 25|감추고자 하면 더욱 큰 의심을 살 뿐이다. 사마표는 어쭙잖은 조심성으로 일을 망칠 생각은 추호도 없었다.
 26|
 27|- 저기, 주군.
 28|
 29|조심스러운 태산의 전음이 귓가를 파고든다. 사마표는 내색하지 않으며 한구석에 자리한 소면 가게를 가리켰다.
 30|
 31|“오늘따라 소면이 당기는구나. 어찌, 한 그릇 하고 가겠느냐?”
 32|
 33|“으응?”
 34|
 35|“배가 부른 녀석이로군. 싫으면 말거라.”
 36|
 37|“아니다! 태산이, 소면 좋다!”
 38|
 39|“진작 그럴 것이지. 이보시오. 소면 열 그릇…… 아니, 스무 개만 말아 주시오.”
 40|
 41|주인인 중년 아낙이 귀를 의심하는 표정으로 되물었다.
 42|
 43|“……몇 그릇이라고 하셨습니까?”
 44|
 45|사마표가 굳이 소면 가게를 택한 이유는 간단했다.
 46|
 47|목이 좋지 않아서인지 손님도 없었고, 다른 사람의 이목을 등진 채 전음을 나눌 수 있기 때문이었다.
 48|
 49|물론 주인장이 무림과는 아무 연관도 없어 보이는, 평범한 양민이라는 점도 한몫했다.
 50|
 51|“스무 그릇이라고 했소. 보시다시피 아귀(餓鬼) 같은 놈이 하나 있어서.”
 52|
 53|“아, 아, 예!”
 54|
 55|그에게는 때아닌 횡재였을 것이다. 눈을 번쩍 뜬 주인장이 바쁘게 손을 놀리는 동안 사마표는 입술을 달싹였다.
 56|
 57|- 할 말이 있던 것 같은데.
 58|
 59|육중한 무게를 지탱하고 있는 작은 의자가 삐걱거린다. 위태롭게 자세를 잡은 태산이 답했다.
 60|
 61|- 주군. 태산이. 불안하다.
 62|
 63|- 무엇이?
 64|
 65|- 무, 문주님의 명을 따르지 않았다. 태산이. 주군 걱정된다.
 66|
 67|순간 사마표의 입가에 고소가 맺혔다.
 68|
 69|- 설마 했는데, 역시 그분 때문이었느냐.
 70|
 71|- 불복하면 좋지 않다. 문주님 화낸다. 주군 위태롭다.
 72|
 73|- 그래, 능히 그러고도 남으실 분이지.
 74|
 75|사마표는 탁자 위에 가지런히 놓인 젓가락을 내려다보았다.
 76|
 77|문득 자신의 아버지인 흑야왕 사마공이 생각난다. 자식을 향한 부정(父情) 따위는 없는 분.
 78|
 79|아마도 그의 아비는 자식을 이 젓가락처럼 생각하고 있을 것이다.
 80|
 81|‘땅에 떨어지면 바꾸고, 마음에 안 들면 치우고.’
 82|
 83|일곱 명의 형과 아홉 명의 누이 역시 그렇게 버려졌다. 사마표는 흑룡마문의 문주가 택한 마지막이자, 가장 잘 만들어진 젓가락이었다.
 84|
 85|‘그마저도 언제 바뀔지 모르지.’
 86|
 87|이미 팔순을 훌쩍 넘긴 노인이지만 식욕도, 성욕도 왕성한 아버지다.
 88|
 89|삼처사첩(三妻四妾)으로도 모자라 열 명이 넘는 첩을 두었으니 위로도, 밑으로도 피가 이어진 혈육이 수두룩했다.
 90|
 91|하지만.
 92|
 93|- 걱정 말거라.
 94|
 95|- 으응?
 96|
 97|사마표는 주인장이 내놓은 미지근한 물을 한 모금 삼켰다.
 98|
 99|- 비정하신 분이지만, 그렇기에 나를 쉽게 내치지 못할 테니.
100|
101|흑야왕 사마공은 분명 비정한 사람이다. 그러니 부모의 정 따위는 내다 버린 채 현실을 냉정히 바라볼 수 있었다.
102|
103|소싯적의 자신을 뛰어넘는 무재(武才)와 깊은 심계(審計)를 지닌 사마표를 대체할 후계자는 없다는 것 역시 같은 맥락이었다.
104|
105|그리고…….
106|
107|- 아무런 문책도 없을 게다. 길이 달라졌을 뿐, 이것 역시 아버지가 원하는 곳을 향하고 있으니까.
108|
109|- 주군. 이해 안 된다. 태산이 머리 나쁘다.
110|
111|자신이 한 말을 이해하지 못해 고개만 갸웃거리는 태산을 향해, 사마표는 빙긋 웃어 보였다.
112|
113|- 굳이 이해할 필요 없으니, 내 옆에만 있거라. 알겠느냐?
114|
115|- 태산이. 주군 말 듣는다. 착하다.
116|
117|태산이 힘차게 고개를 끄덕인 그때, 주인장이 소면이 가득 담긴 그릇들을 탁자에 올려놓기 시작했다.
118|
119|“뜨거우니 천천히…….”
120|
121|“우와! 태산이! 잘 먹겠습니다!”
122|
123|“에그머니나!”
124|
125|깜짝 놀라는 주인장과 김이 펄펄 나는 소면을 그릇 채 들고 삼키는 태산.
126|
127|그 모습을 바라보며 피식 웃던 사마표의 얼굴이, 순간 딱딱하게 굳었다.
128|
129|“음.”
130|
131|정신없이 젓가락을 놀리던 태산이 고개를 쳐들었다.
132|
133|“주군. 왜 그러나?”
134|
135|“…….”
136|
137|“주군?”
138|
139|태산의 물음에도 말없이 어딘가를 응시하던 사마표가 작게 중얼거렸다.
140|
141|“아니다. 아무것도. 잘못 본 모양이야.”
142|
143|하지만 사마표는 알고 있었다. 스치듯 지나쳐 간 한 사람의 모습은 결코 잘못 본 것이 아니라는 것을.
144|
145|그리고 그것이 무엇을 의미하는지를.
146|
147|“……그냥 고분고분하게 명을 따를 걸 그랬나.”
148|
149|“응? 주군. 뭐라고 했나?”
150|
151|사마표는 대답 대신 한숨을 내쉬었다. 어느새 태산의 손에는 마지막 그릇이 들려 있었다.
152|
153|“염치도 없는 녀석 같으니. 마저 처먹어라.”
154|
155|“와! 태산이! 주군을 위해 목숨을 바친다!”
156|
157|
158|
159|* * *
160|
161|
162|
163|“자, 여기요.”
164|
165|영창 피아노보다 맑고 고운 목소리. 이쪽을 향해 불쑥 내민 손에는 두 개의 죽간이 들려 있다.
166|
167|‘이게 무슨 상황이지.’
168|
169|흑룡마문의 두 불청객이 떠나고, 적천강이 측간에 간 지 불과 한 식경도 되지 않은 상황.
170|
171|또다시 찾아온 뜻밖의 손님은 갑작스러운 것을 넘어 당황스럽기까지 하다.
172|
173|말없이 눈만 깜빡이던 나는 간신히 목소리를 끄집어냈다.
174|
175|“이……게 뭡니까?”
176|
177|“지원서죠.”
178|
179|당연한 걸 왜 묻느냐는 표정으로 대답한 주화란이 덧붙였다.
180|
181|“저와 여기 있는 송 호위의 것까지 두 개예요.”
182|
183|뒤에 서 있던 송일섬이 작게 중얼거렸다.
184|
185|“난 동의한 적 없는데.”
186|
187|“제가 고용했잖아요. 호위라면 당연히 따라와야죠.”
188|
189|“이런 상황은 항목에 없었잖소. 계약 위반이오. 무림맹에 속하게 되면 위험 수당이…….”
190|
191|“두 배 더 드릴게요.”
192|
193|“그럼 이야기가 달라지지.”
194|
195|종남파한테 뜯어 낸 돈이 많아서 그런가, 영 앤 리치의 시원시원한 플렉스를 보여 주는 주화란이다.
196|
197|물론 지켜보는 나로서는 한여름 온실에 들어온 것처럼 갑갑했지만.
198|
199|“그럼. 정말로?”
200|
201|“네. 정말로.”
202|
203|내 물음에 망설임 없이 고개를 끄덕인 주화란이 투명한 눈동자로 나를 응시했다.
204|
205|“이룡각에 들어가고 싶어요.”
206|
207|“……!”
208|
209|짐작은 했지만, 막상 주화란에게서 직접 듣자 입 안이 까끌거렸다. 잠시 생각하던 나는 입을 열었다.
210|
211|“인연이 있다고 해서 받아 줄 생각은 없습니다.”
212|
213|“처음부터 그럴 생각이었다면 지원서도 없이 왔겠죠?”
214|
215|싱긋 웃으며 대답하는 주화란의 모습에 내심 한숨이 흘러나왔다.
216|
217|“위험할 겁니다. 그것도 매우.”
218|
219|“이미 알고 왔어요. 맹주부 직속에, 다른 각주들과는 달리 휘하에 단과 대도 거느리지 못하는 이룡각. 아마 별동대의 성격이 강하겠죠.”
220|
221|정답이다.
222|
223|매종학은 무림맹 내부에서도 상당한 전력인 나와 청풍을 소규모 별동대로 운용하길 바랐고, 그것은 대다수의 수뇌부가 고개를 끄덕이게 만든 이유이기도 했다.
224|
225|“주 소저, 그걸 알면서도 왜…….”
226|
227|“진 대협.”
228|
229|내가 말을 끝맺기도 전에, 주화란이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
230|
231|“다른 지원자들에게도 그렇게 말씀하셨나요?”
232|
233|“네?”
234|
235|“위험하다. 알면서도 왜 지원하느냐.”
236|
237|나직한 목소리가 이어졌다.
238|
239|“이상하네요. 사람이 필요해서 방을 붙이셨을 텐데, 이렇게 만류하시니.”
240|
241|“그건…….”
242|
243|망설이는 나를 보며 주화란이 피식 웃었다.
244|
245|“할 말 없으시죠?”
246|
247|정곡이다. 뒤통수를 긁적인 나는 어쩔 수 없이 고개를 끄덕였다.
248|
249|“솔직히, 예. 그러네요.”
250|
251|“저는 이곳에 한 사람의 무인으로 왔으니, 진 대협께서도 있는 그대로를 봐 주셨으면 좋겠네요.”
252|
253|“있는 그대로라…….”
254|
255|“진 대협 눈에는 턱없이 부족할지 모르겠지만, 저 역시 절정의 경지에 오른 검객이에요.”
256|
257|“기왕 솔직한 거, 터놓고 말씀드리면 많이 부족하긴 합니다. 송일섬. 저 녀석이라면 모를까.”
258|
259|쿡.
260|
261|숨죽인 채 상황을 지켜보던 혁무진이 슬쩍 옆구리를 찔렀다.
262|
263|하지만 그건 녀석의 과한 우려에 불과하다. 그 증거로, 내 직설적인 말에도 주화란의 눈빛은 흔들리지 않았다.
264|
265|“다른 지원자들에 비해서도 그런가요?”
266|
267|“글쎄요. 장담할 수는 없지만 아마 그럴 겁니다.”
268|
269|“경험은요?”
270|
271|“경험?”
272|
273|“저는 열두 살 때부터 아버지를 따라 표행(鏢行)을 나갔어요. 연륜과 천하의 지리에 관해서는 여느 노강호와 비교해도 떨어지지 않는다고 생각해요.”
274|
275|맞다. 주화란은 한때 천하에서도 손꼽히던 용봉표국의 후계자였다.
276|
277|근 몇 년 동안은 주화입마로 쓰러진 아버지 대신 직접 표국을 이끌기도 했다.
278|
279|‘그를 통해 얻은 경험은…… 확실히 무시 못 하지.’
280|
281|표국은 천하 곳곳을 방랑하는 집단이다. 의뢰를 기간에 맞춰 완수하기 위해 수단과 방법을 가리지 않는 그들은 천하 곳곳의 길과 정보를 알고 있다.
282|
283|하물며 주화란의 조부인 표왕(鏢王)은 과거 정마대전 당시, 마교의 수많은 이목을 피해 만리행(萬里行)을 성공시키기도 했었다.
284|
285|“진 대협.”
286|
287|힘 있는 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
288|
289|“짐이 될 생각은 추호도 없어요. 다만 진 대협께서도 냉정하게 생각해 주세요. 지금까지 있었던 모든 인연을 떠나, 저와 여기 있는 송 호위가 정말 이룡각에 필요 없는 존재인지.”
290|
291|“……!”
292|
293|“각오는 충분히 했어요. 떨어트리신다고 해도 감수할게요.”
294|
295|나는 지그시 눈을 감았다.
296|
297|주화란의 말이 맞다. 이건 냉정하게 생각해야 할 문제다.
298|
299|지금 내 대답을 기다리고 있는 사람은 어느 날 밤, 이제 막 꽃을 피우기 시작한 정원에서 함께 걷던 여인이 아니었다.
300|
301|‘은비화(隱匕花) 주화란.’
302|
303|십봉룡으로 인정받을 만큼 상당한 무위를 지닌 한 사람의 무인이고, 용봉표국의 소국주다.
304|
305|게다가 사실상 별동대나 다름없는 이룡각의 향후 임무 수행에 필요한 여러 가지 능력을 갖추기도 했다.
306|

“I want to join the Two Dragons Pavilion.”

[P94]
“…!”

[P95]
I had suspected as much, but hearing Ju Hwaran say it herself left my mouth dry. I thought for a moment before speaking.

[P96]
“I won’t accept you just because we know each other.”

[P97]
“If I’d expected that, I would’ve come without an application, wouldn’t I?”

[P98]
She smiled. I sighed inwardly.

[P99]
“It’ll be dangerous. Very dangerous.”

[P100]
“I know. The Two Dragons Pavilion serves directly under the Alliance Leader’s Office, but unlike the other pavilions, it doesn’t even have its own regiments or squads. You’ll probably operate more like a small detached force.”

[P101]
Exactly right.

[P102]
Mae Jonghak wanted to deploy Cheongpung and me, two considerable assets even within the Murim Alliance, as a small detached force. It was also why most of the leadership had agreed to the arrangement.

[P103]
“Young Lady Ju, if you know that, why—”

[P104]
“Great Hero Jin.”

[P105]
Ju Hwaran cut me off.

[P106]
“Did you say that to the other applicants?”

[P107]
“What?”

[P108]
“That it’s dangerous. Did you ask why they were applying when they knew that?”

[P109]
Her quiet voice went on.

[P110]
“It’s strange. You put up a notice because you needed people, and now you’re trying to talk me out of it.”

[P111]
“That’s…”

[P112]
She gave a quiet laugh when I hesitated.

[P113]
“You don’t have an answer, do you?”

[P114]
She had me there. I scratched the back of my head and reluctantly nodded.

[P115]
“Honestly? No, I don’t.”

[P116]
“I came here as a martial artist. I’d like you to judge me as one.”

[P117]
“As a martial artist…”

[P118]
“I might fall far short by your standards, but I’m a swordswoman who has reached the Peak realm.”

[P119]
“Since we’re being honest, you do fall pretty far short. Song Ilseom might be another story.”

[P120]
Poke.

[P121]
Hyuk Mujin, who had been watching with bated breath, gave me a discreet jab in the ribs.

[P122]
He needn’t have worried. Ju Hwaran’s gaze did not waver.

[P123]
“Even compared with the other applicants?”

[P124]
“I can’t say for certain, but probably.”

[P125]
“What about experience?”

[P126]
“Experience?”

[P127]
“I started accompanying my father on escort runs when I was twelve. In experience and knowledge of the land, I don’t think I fall short of any seasoned veteran of the martial world.”

[P128]
She had a point. Ju Hwaran had been heir to the Yongbong Escort Bureau, once among the most renowned escort bureaus in the world. For the past several years, she had even run it herself after her father collapsed from qi deviation.

[P129]
*I can’t dismiss the experience she gained from that.*

[P130]
Escort bureaus traveled far and wide. To complete their assignments on time, they used whatever means they could, learning the roads and gathering information wherever they went.

[P131]
And during the Great Faction War, Ju Hwaran’s grandfather, the Escort King, had completed his legendary Ten-Thousand-Li Journey while evading the Demonic Cult’s countless watchers.

[P132]
“Great Hero Jin.”

[P133]
Her voice was firm.

[P134]
“I have no intention of becoming a burden. But please think about this objectively. Set aside everything that’s happened between us until now. Are Captain Song and I truly of no use to the Two Dragons Pavilion?”

[P135]
“…!”

[P136]
“I’ve thought it through. If you reject me, I’ll accept it.”

[P137]
I closed my eyes.

[P138]
Ju Hwaran was right. I needed to think about this without letting my feelings get in the way.

[P139]
The person waiting for my answer was not the woman I had walked beside one night in a garden where the flowers were just beginning to bloom.

[P140]
*Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.*

[P141]
She was a martial artist skilled enough to be counted among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, and the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P142]
She also had abilities we would need on the missions ahead, given that the Two Dragons Pavilion would operate as a detached force.

[P143]
*Then why?*

[P144]
Why did I hate admitting it? Why did I want to stop her, even if I had to be unreasonable?

[P145]
“Um, Captain.”

[P146]
I opened my eyes. Hyuk Mujin watched me nervously before going on.

[P147]
“I think you’ve forgotten something.”

[P148]
“What?”

[P149]
“All the other applicants ran away. Every last one. They probably won’t come back tomorrow or the day after, either.”

[P150]
“I know, you punk. Old Man Ilyang got carried out of here half-paralyzed. So?”

[P151]
“No, I mean… that’s all I wanted to say.”

[P152]
Hyuk Mujin flinched and turned his head away.

[P153]
But I understood him perfectly.

[P154]
“Whew.”

[P155]
I sighed and looked straight at Ju Hwaran.

[P156]
“Before I answer, there’s something you should know.”

[P157]
How was I supposed to bring it up? As I hesitated, she smiled.

[P158]
“It doesn’t matter.”

[P159]
“What?”

[P160]
“I saw them on my way here. With someone that big beside him, how could I miss them? And from what people were whispering, I could more or less tell where they’d come from.”

[P161]
Ju Hwaran continued calmly.

[P162]
“Why would that be a problem?”

[P163]
“…!”

[P164]
“I think I’ve given you enough time to consider it. May I have your answer?”

[P165]
I studied her. The tangle in my head seemed to have cleared.

[P166]
Or perhaps it hadn’t, not entirely.

[P167]
But right now, at least, I knew what I had to say.

[P168]
“Yes. All right.”

[P169]
A bright smile spread across Ju Hwaran’s face.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

*—He is heartless. That is precisely why he cannot easily cast me aside.*

[P48]
Black Night King Sima Gong was indeed a heartless man. He could set aside parental affection and assess reality with a cold eye.

[P49]
And the reality was that he had no other successor capable of replacing Sama Pyo, whose martial talent surpassed even Sima Gong’s at his age and whose mind was every bit as calculating.

[P50]
Besides…

[P51]
*—There will be no punishment. I’ve taken a different route, but it still leads where my father wants to go.*

[P52]
*—My lord. Taishan does not understand. Taishan is stupid.*

[P53]
Sama Pyo smiled at Taishan, who could only tilt his head in confusion.

[P54]
*—You don’t need to understand. Just stay by my side. All right?*

[P55]
*—Taishan listens to my lord. Taishan is good.*

[P56]
Taishan nodded vigorously. Just then, the owner began setting bowls piled high with thin noodles on the table.

[P57]
“Careful, they’re hot. Take your time—”

[P58]
“Wow! Taishan! Thank you for the food!”

[P59]
“Oh my goodness!”

[P60]
The owner stared in shock as Taishan lifted a bowl of steaming noodles and gulped them down.

[P61]
Sama Pyo let out a quiet laugh at the sight. Then his face went rigid.

[P62]
“Hmm.”

[P63]
Taishan looked up from his noodles.

[P64]
“My lord. What is it?”

[P65]
“…”

[P66]
“My lord?”

[P67]
Still staring at something, Sama Pyo murmured, “No. Nothing. I must have seen wrong.”

[P68]
But he knew he had not mistaken the person who had passed by. He knew what that person’s presence meant, too.

[P69]
“…Perhaps I should have just obeyed the order.”

[P70]
“Hm? My lord. What did you say?”

[P71]
Sama Pyo answered with a sigh. Taishan already had the last bowl in his hands.

[P72]
“You shameless glutton. Finish stuffing your face.”

[P73]
“Wow! Taishan will give his life for my lord!”

[P74]
* * *

[P75]
“Here you go.”

[P76]
A voice clearer and lovelier than a Young Chang piano.[^1] A hand held out two bamboo slips to me.

[P77]
*What’s going on?*

[P78]
Less than half an hour had passed since the two uninvited guests from the Black Dragon Demon Gate had left and Jeok Cheongang had gone to the latrine. Now another unexpected visitor had appeared, and this one left me at a loss.

[P79]
I blinked at her, then finally managed to speak.

[P80]
“W-What are these?”

[P81]
“Applications.”

[P82]
Ju Hwaran looked as though she wondered why I had to ask. “One for me and one for Captain Song.”

[P83]
Behind her, Song Ilseom muttered, “I never agreed to this.”

[P84]
“I hired you, didn’t I? If you’re my escort, of course you have to come with me.”

[P85]
“This wasn’t in the contract. It’s a breach of contract. If I join the Murim Alliance, I’ll need hazard pay…”

[P86]
“I’ll pay you double.”

[P87]
“Then that’s a different story.”

[P88]
Maybe it was all the money she had wrung out of the Zhongnan Sect. Ju Hwaran was showing off the sort of easy spending only someone young and rich could manage.

[P89]
Watching her, though, I felt as stifled as if I’d stepped into a greenhouse in midsummer.

[P90]
“So. You’re serious?”

[P91]
“Yes. I am.”

[P92]
Ju Hwaran nodded without hesitation and met my eyes.

[P93]
“I want to join the Two Dragons Pavilion.”

[P94]
“…!”

[P95]
I had suspected as much, but hearing Ju Hwaran say it herself left my mouth dry. I thought for a moment before speaking.

[P96]
“I won’t accept you just because we know each other.”

[P97]
“If I’d expected that, I would’ve come without an application, wouldn’t I?”

[P98]
She smiled. I sighed inwardly.

[P99]
“It’ll be dangerous. Very dangerous.”

[P100]
“I know. The Two Dragons Pavilion serves directly under the Alliance Leader’s Office, but unlike the other pavilions, it doesn’t even have its own regiments or squads. You’ll probably operate more like a small detached force.”

[P101]
Exactly right.

[P102]
Mae Jonghak wanted to deploy Cheongpung and me, two considerable assets even within the Murim Alliance, as a small detached force. It was also why most of the leadership had agreed to the arrangement.

[P103]
“Young Lady Ju, if you know that, why—”

[P104]
“Great Hero Jin.”

[P105]
Ju Hwaran cut me off.

[P106]
“Did you say that to the other applicants?”

[P107]
“What?”

[P108]
“That it’s dangerous. Did you ask why they were applying when they knew that?”

[P109]
Her quiet voice went on.

[P110]
“It’s strange. You put up a notice because you needed people, and now you’re trying to talk me out of it.”

[P111]
“That’s…”

[P112]
She gave a quiet laugh when I hesitated.

[P113]
“You don’t have an answer, do you?”

[P114]
She had me there. I scratched the back of my head and reluctantly nodded.

[P115]
“Honestly? No, I don’t.”

[P116]
“I came here as a martial artist. I’d like you to judge me as one.”

[P117]
“As a martial artist…”

[P118]
“I might fall far short by your standards, but I’m a swordswoman who has reached the Peak realm.”

[P119]
“Since we’re being honest, you do fall pretty far short. Song Ilseom might be another story.”

[P120]
Poke.

[P121]
Hyuk Mujin, who had been watching with bated breath, gave me a discreet jab in the ribs.

[P122]
He needn’t have worried. Ju Hwaran’s gaze did not waver.

[P123]
“Even compared with the other applicants?”

[P124]
“I can’t say for certain, but probably.”

[P125]
“What about experience?”

[P126]
“Experience?”

[P127]
“I started accompanying my father on escort runs when I was twelve. In experience and knowledge of the land, I don’t think I fall short of any seasoned veteran of the martial world.”

[P128]
She had a point. Ju Hwaran had been heir to the Yongbong Escort Bureau, once among the most renowned escort bureaus in the world. For the past several years, she had even run it herself after her father collapsed from qi deviation.

[P129]
*I can’t dismiss the experience she gained from that.*

[P130]
Escort bureaus traveled far and wide. To complete their assignments on time, they used whatever means they could, learning the roads and gathering information wherever they went.

[P131]
And during the Great Faction War, Ju Hwaran’s grandfather, the Escort King, had completed his legendary Ten-Thousand-Li Journey while evading the Demonic Cult’s countless watchers.

[P132]
“Great Hero Jin.”

[P133]
Her voice was firm.

[P134]
“I have no intention of becoming a burden. But please think about this objectively. Set aside everything that’s happened between us until now. Are Captain Song and I truly of no use to the Two Dragons Pavilion?”

[P135]
“…!”

[P136]
“I’ve thought it through. If you reject me, I’ll accept it.”

[P137]
I closed my eyes.

[P138]
Ju Hwaran was right. I needed to think about this without letting my feelings get in the way.

[P139]
The person waiting for my answer was not the woman I had walked beside one night in a garden where the flowers were just beginning to bloom.

[P140]
*Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.*

[P141]
She was a martial artist skilled enough to be counted among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, and the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P142]
She also had abilities we would need on the missions ahead, given that the Two Dragons Pavilion would operate as a detached force.

[P143]
*Then why?*

[P144]
Why did I hate admitting it? Why did I want to stop her, even if I had to be unreasonable?

[P145]
“Um, Captain.”

[P146]
I opened my eyes. Hyuk Mujin watched me nervously before going on.

[P147]
“I think you’ve forgotten something.”

[P148]
“What?”

[P149]
“All the other applicants ran away. Every last one. They probably won’t come back tomorrow or the day after, either.”

[P150]
“I know, you punk. Old Man Ilyang got carried out of here half-paralyzed. So?”

[P151]
“No, I mean… that’s all I wanted to say.”

[P152]
Hyuk Mujin flinched and turned his head away.

[P153]
But I understood him perfectly.

[P154]
“Whew.”

[P155]
I sighed and looked straight at Ju Hwaran.

[P156]
“Before I answer, there’s something you should know.”

[P157]
How was I supposed to bring it up? As I hesitated, she smiled.

[P158]
“It doesn’t matter.”

[P159]
“What?”

[P160]
“I saw them on my way here. With someone that big beside him, how could I miss them? And from what people were whispering, I could more or less tell where they’d come from.”

[P161]
Ju Hwaran continued calmly.

[P162]
“Why would that be a problem?”

[P163]
“…!”

[P164]
“I think I’ve given you enough time to consider it. May I have your answer?”

[P165]
I studied her. The tangle in my head seemed to have cleared.

[P166]
Or perhaps it hadn’t, not entirely.

[P167]
But right now, at least, I knew what I had to say.

[P168]
“Yes. All right.”

[P169]
A bright smile spread across Ju Hwaran’s face.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“Since we’re being honest, you do fall pretty far short. Song Ilseom might be another story.”

[P120]
Poke.

[P121]
Hyuk Mujin, who had been watching with bated breath, gave me a discreet jab in the ribs.

[P122]
He needn’t have worried. Ju Hwaran’s gaze did not waver.

[P123]
“Even compared with the other applicants?”

[P124]
“I can’t say for certain, but probably.”

[P125]
“What about experience?”

[P126]
“Experience?”

[P127]
“I started accompanying my father on escort runs when I was twelve. In experience and knowledge of the land, I don’t think I fall short of any seasoned veteran of the martial world.”

[P128]
She had a point. Ju Hwaran had been heir to the Yongbong Escort Bureau, once among the most renowned escort bureaus in the world. For the past several years, she had even run it herself after her father collapsed from qi deviation.

[P129]
*I can’t dismiss the experience she gained from that.*

[P130]
Escort bureaus traveled far and wide. To complete their assignments on time, they used whatever means they could, learning the roads and gathering information wherever they went.

[P131]
And during the Great Faction War, Ju Hwaran’s grandfather, the Escort King, had completed his legendary Ten-Thousand-Li Journey while evading the Demonic Cult’s countless watchers.

[P132]
“Great Hero Jin.”

[P133]
Her voice was firm.

[P134]
“I have no intention of becoming a burden. But please think about this objectively. Set aside everything that’s happened between us until now. Are Captain Song and I truly of no use to the Two Dragons Pavilion?”

[P135]
“…!”

[P136]
“I’ve thought it through. If you reject me, I’ll accept it.”

[P137]
I closed my eyes.

[P138]
Ju Hwaran was right. I needed to think about this without letting my feelings get in the way.

[P139]
The person waiting for my answer was not the woman I had walked beside one night in a garden where the flowers were just beginning to bloom.

[P140]
*Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.*

[P141]
She was a martial artist skilled enough to be counted among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, and the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P142]
She also had abilities we would need on the missions ahead, given that the Two Dragons Pavilion would operate as a detached force.

[P143]
*Then why?*

[P144]
Why did I hate admitting it? Why did I want to stop her, even if I had to be unreasonable?

[P145]
“Um, Captain.”

[P146]
I opened my eyes. Hyuk Mujin watched me nervously before going on.

[P147]
“I think you’ve forgotten something.”

[P148]
“What?”

[P149]
“All the other applicants ran away. Every last one. They probably won’t come back tomorrow or the day after, either.”

[P150]
“I know, you punk. Old Man Ilyang got carried out of here half-paralyzed. So?”

[P151]
“No, I mean… that’s all I wanted to say.”

[P152]
Hyuk Mujin flinched and turned his head away.

[P153]
But I understood him perfectly.

[P154]
“Whew.”

[P155]
I sighed and looked straight at Ju Hwaran.

[P156]
“Before I answer, there’s something you should know.”

[P157]
How was I supposed to bring it up? As I hesitated, she smiled.

[P158]
“It doesn’t matter.”

[P159]
“What?”

[P160]
“I saw them on my way here. With someone that big beside him, how could I miss them? And from what people were whispering, I could more or less tell where they’d come from.”

[P161]
Ju Hwaran continued calmly.

[P162]
“Why would that be a problem?”

[P163]
“…!”

[P164]
“I think I’ve given you enough time to consider it. May I have your answer?”

[P165]
I studied her. The tangle in my head seemed to have cleared.

[P166]
Or perhaps it hadn’t, not entirely.

[P167]
But right now, at least, I knew what I had to say.

[P168]
“Yes. All right.”

[P169]
A bright smile spread across Ju Hwaran’s face.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
